feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 3 (body_length 0.12, mass 0.5, wheel_track 0.10) scored 46.71, below iterations 1 and 2 (50.13, 50.07). Line loss stayed at 1 per track, max_error stayed at 0.0613 to 0.0668, and s-bend progress fell from 0.15 to 0.13. Narrowing the track and shortening the body therefore did not help turning, so I have reverted those values to iteration 2. Iterations 0 to 2 showed that span, footprint and lead do not change max_error by more than 0.001 m. The steady drift pattern suggests a fixed motor-mismatch bias, which I am testing with ki 0.3 in the controller. The result will therefore show the joint effect of your footprint change and my integral change. Interpret the next race as follows. If max_error falls below 0.06 and line_loss_events reaches 0 or 1 on the s-bend and slalom, keep sensor_size 0.012 and the iteration 2 body. If max_error stays at 0.061 to 0.069 with line loss at 1, the footprint is not the limit, so change speed next (wheel_radius). Do not change body or track again, because iteration 3 showed no benefit.
requested_changes: Keep the body and drivetrain at the iteration 2 values (body_length 0.18, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12) and keep the sensor layout at x = -0.03 to 0.03 m, y = 0.04 m. If the next race still shows max_error from 0.061 to 0.069 with one line-loss event per track, raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m. Iterations 0 to 3 show progress stuck at 0.10 to 0.15 with no completions, so speed is the next untested lever once the drift is addressed.

If line_loss_events falls to 0 and max_error stays below 0.06 with sensor_size 0.012, keep 0.012 m and do not change the sensor span again. Iterations 0 to 2 showed that span changes do not move max_error, so further span changes are unlikely to help.
